decisions.reason: Although it draws on some biomass-related knowledge, a consumer superfood drink sits farther from the firm's core industrial technology, customer base and commercialization routines, so absorptive capacity is weaker and resources are better redeployed.

Modular waste-to-energy extensions fit the firm's established engineering and plant offer very closely, letting it use existing knowledge, installed-customer relationships and in-house R&D to refine the product.

A waste-oil-to-energy plant is strongly aligned with the firm's core waste-to-energy capabilities and its dedicated product-page presence suggests sufficient commitment and learning potential to continue.

Plastic-waste-to-fuel is adjacent rather than fully core, but it still builds on related conversion, prototyping and automation knowledge that the firm's R&D and research partnerships can absorb and improve.
